public_rationale: The available comparisons do not settle this broad claim. Epoch estimates a narrow OpenAI lead among major AI labs at the end of 2025, but its uncertainty overlaps DeepMind’s and its measure is compute use rather than total requirements. A rival’s larger individual cluster would not establish a larger organizational total. No decisive counterexample was established, and finite evidence cannot prove perpetuity.
limitations: The ranking depends on the meaning of requirements and the organizational boundary.
Year-end 2025 estimates do not establish the April 2025 historical assertion.

our_interpretation: Read as a claim that OpenAI’s total organizational compute requirement exceeds every other organization’s historical requirement and will retain that position indefinitely.
Compare total compute across research, training, and inference, including rented capacity. A single cluster, hardware ownership, spending, or announced construction is not the same measure.
Comparable deployed computing capacity can inform requirements, but does not automatically measure unmet demand.
In perpetuity supplies no finite deadline. The present-tense assertion is retained as part of the continuing claim.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence establishes the claimed historical maximum and its continuation. Finite observations can support a bounded portion but cannot establish perpetuity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A dated, comparable organizational measurement establishes that OpenAI did not hold the claimed maximum at publication or subsequently ceased to hold it; permanent cessation of its compute-requiring operations would also contradict continuation.
